Author: Simon Charette <charette.s@gmail.com>

    Fixed #31395 -- Made setUpTestData enforce in-memory data isolation.
    
    Since it's introduction in Django 1.8 setUpTestData has been suffering
    from a documented but confusing caveat due to its sharing of attributes
    assigned during its execution with all test instances.
    
    By keeping track of class attributes assigned during the setUpTestData
    phase its possible to ensure only deep copies are provided to test
    instances on attribute retreival and prevent manual setUp gymnastic to
    work around the previous lack of in-memory data isolation.
    
    Thanks Adam Johnson for the extensive review.

I have investigated and resolved the issue where deferred fields are incorrect when following prefetches back to the parent object.

### Root Cause
In [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365), and [`create_reverse_many_to_one_manager.get_prefetch_queryset`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L633), the prefetcher iterates through `queryset` to manually set the reverse relation cache pointing back to the parent `instance`.

When an inner prefetch back to the parent object was executed (e.g. `Prefetch("user", queryset=User.objects.only("kind"))`), or when the parent instance had deferred fields (e.g. `User.objects.only("email")`):
1. The reverse descriptor unconditionally overwrote any existing cached related object on `rel_obj` even if it had already been cached by the prefetch.
2. The reverse descriptor cached parent instances that had deferred fields onto `rel_obj`, causing `rel_obj` to reference an incomplete instance rather than allowing subsequent lookups or attribute accesses to load the complete/prefetched instance.

### Solution
In [`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py):
- Before assigning the parent `instance` into the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj`, ensure:
  1. The relation is not already cached on `rel_obj` (`not is_cached(rel_obj)`).
  2. The parent `instance` does not have deferred fields (`not instance.get_deferred_fields()`).
